reason: No port. Shadowing means a declaration whose name is already bound in an enclosing scope (imports, params, var/let/const, classes, type params, with temporal-dead-zone and ignore-* options). This is binding resolution across scopes with name identity, which neither relations (fresh metavariable env) nor single patterns (anchor on the outer node) can express.

evidence.why: `let a = 2; // failure` in an if-block shadows `var a` from line 14. The anchor is the inner name, and matching it requires binding `a` from an outer declaration
`let c = 2;` looks the same syntactically but is not a failure: no outer `c` exists
